items.stem: Why is 'the output should look good' a poor quality criterion for an automated gate?

options.text: It is not measurable, so a machine cannot verify it
options.rationale: Correct: gates need verifiable criteria a check can evaluate.

options.text: It is too strict for any model
options.rationale: The problem is vagueness, not strictness.
Token usage is unrelated to the criterion's measurability.
It can matter, but it must be made measurable to gate on.

items.explanation: Correct: gates need verifiable criteria a check can evaluate.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO belong in a robust AI output quality gate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Schema validation that rejects malformed structure
options.rationale: Correct: schema checks catch structurally invalid output.

options.text: A correctness or grounding check beyond format
options.rationale: Correct: format alone does not confirm the content is right.

options.text: Only a check that the response is non-empty
options.rationale: Non-empty is far too weak to be the only check.

options.text: No checks, trusting the model fully
options.rationale: Trusting output ungated defeats the purpose of a gate.

items.explanation: Correct: schema checks catch structurally invalid output.

items.stem: Output fails a required check in the gate. What should a well-designed gate do?

options.text: Block the output and route it to a fallback, bounded retry or human review
options.rationale: Correct: a gate must stop failing output and route it, not merely warn.

options.text: Pass it through with a warning in the logs
options.rationale: A warning-only gate still ships bad output.
Unbounded retries can loop and overspend.

options.text: Delete the check so it passes
options.rationale: Removing the check defeats the gate.

items.explanation: Correct: a gate must stop failing output and route it, not merely warn.
